children.text: Fermentation produces dissolved carbon dioxide obeying Henry law \(c_\ell=k_HP_{CO_2}\). Use surface tension \(\sigma=47\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{J/m^2}\), liquid density \(\rho_\ell=1000\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), \(k_H(20\,{}^\circ\mathrm C)=3.3\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,Pa^{-1}}\), \(k_H(6\,{}^\circ\mathrm C)=5.4\times10^{-4}\) in the same units, \(P_0=10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}\), ideal-gas exponent gamma=1.3, \(g_0=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\), and R=8.314 J/(mol K). This problem is a physics model of nucleation, sound and gas expansion. Part A is at T0=20 degrees Celsius, with liquid pressure P0, constant temperature and only CO2 inside the bubbles. Write \(c_0=k_HP_0\).
Find the pressure Pb inside a spherical bubble of radius a.
The dissolved concentration far away is cl and at the bubble surface cb=kH Pb. Find the critical radius above which growth occurs and evaluate it for cl=4c0.

children.text: Bubbles detach at frequency fb=20 Hz and rise at instantaneous terminal speed. With Stokes drag \(6\pi\eta av\), find the main forces and v(a). Estimate viscosity from the original bubble train and millimetre scale.
With constant growth rate qa, find radius aH after rising height Hl, assuming aH much greater than a0. Evaluate for Hl=10 cm and the graph growth rate.
For Nb nucleation sites, each emitting at fb, liquid volume Vl and height Hl, find the differential equation and characteristic concentration-decay time. Neglect free-surface diffusion and a0.

children.text: A piston mass mp moves in an aperture of area S above an ideal-gas cavity of equilibrium volume V0 and pressure P0. Small outward displacement z changes volume by Sz. Find frequency neglecting gravity.

For the bursting bubble, \(V_0=4\pi a^3/3\), aperture radius r and \(m_p=8\rho_gr^3/3\), \(\rho_g=1.8\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\). The aperture grows to \(r_c=2a^2\sqrt{\rho_\ell g_0/\sigma}/\sqrt3\). The maximum acoustic frequency is 40 kHz and bursting time \(t_b=3\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm s\). Find a and film thickness h.

nodes.alt: Original bottleneck dimensions, headspace and two observed fog types.

children.text: A bottle holds total CO2 amount nT=0.2 mol, liquid volume VL=750 mL and gas headspace VG=25 mL containing only CO2. Find equilibrium pressure at 6 and 20 degrees Celsius.

For all subsequent parts use Pi=4.69 bar at 6 degrees Celsius and 7.45 bar at 20 degrees Celsius. The gas expands reversibly and adiabatically to P0. Calculate the final temperatures without phase change. Solid CO2 saturation follows \(\log_{10}(P_{sat}^{CO_2}/P_0)=6.81-1300/(T-3.49)\). Identify grey-white water fog or blue CO2-crystal fog for each initial temperature, assuming the two stated fog mechanisms are exclusive.

At 6 degrees Celsius use Pi=4.69 bar. A cork has mass 10 g, diameter d=1.8 cm, and initially inserted length l0=2.5 cm. Friction is alpha times its contact area. Initially the pressure force barely exceeds friction. Find the maximum rise after exit, neglecting net gas pressure thereafter.

statement.text:
Champagne Bubbles
Fermentation produces dissolved carbon dioxide obeying Henry law \(c_\ell=k_HP_{CO_2}\). Use surface tension \(\sigma=47\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{J/m^2}\), liquid density \(\rho_\ell=1000\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), \(k_H(20\,{}^\circ\mathrm C)=3.3\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,Pa^{-1}}\), \(k_H(6\,{}^\circ\mathrm C)=5.4\times10^{-4}\) in the same units, \(P_0=10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}\), ideal-gas exponent gamma=1.3, \(g_0=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\), and R=8.314 J/(mol K). This problem is a physics model of nucleation, sound and gas expansion. Part A is at T0=20 degrees Celsius, with liquid pressure P0, constant temperature and only CO2 inside the bubbles. Write \(c_0=k_HP_0\).
A.1. Bubble pressure
Find the pressure Pb inside a spherical bubble of radius a.
A.2. Critical nucleation radius
The dissolved concentration far away is cl and at the bubble surface cb=kH Pb. Find the critical radius above which growth occurs and evaluate it for cl=4c0.
A.3. Growth laws

For initial radius a0 about 40 micrometres neglect Laplace pressure. The incoming molar flux is either model 1, \(j=D(c_\ell-c_b)/a\), or model 2, \(j=K(c_\ell-c_b)\). Find nc(a), both growth laws, identify the observed model from the original radius-time plot and evaluate D or K.
A.4. Rising bubble and viscosity

Bubbles detach at frequency fb=20 Hz and rise at instantaneous terminal speed. With Stokes drag \(6\pi\eta av\), find the main forces and v(a). Estimate viscosity from the original bubble train and millimetre scale.
A.5. Radius at the surface
With constant growth rate qa, find radius aH after rising height Hl, assuming aH much greater than a0. Evaluate for Hl=10 cm and the graph growth rate.
A.6. Dissolved-gas decay
For Nb nucleation sites, each emitting at fb, liquid volume Vl and height Hl, find the differential equation and characteristic concentration-decay time. Neglect free-surface diffusion and a0.
B.1. Film retraction speed

A circular hole opens at constant speed vf in a film of thickness h. The exterior film is stationary. Half the released two-surface energy becomes kinetic energy of the rim plus newly collected liquid. Neglect rim-surface growth. Find vf.
B.2. Helmholtz frequency

A piston mass mp moves in an aperture of area S above an ideal-gas cavity of equilibrium volume V0 and pressure P0. Small outward displacement z changes volume by Sz. Find frequency neglecting gravity.
B.3. Bubble film dimensions
For the bursting bubble, \(V_0=4\pi a^3/3\), aperture radius r and \(m_p=8\rho_gr^3/3\), \(\rho_g=1.8\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\). The aperture grows to \(r_c=2a^2\sqrt{\rho_\ell g_0/\sigma}/\sqrt3\). The maximum acoustic frequency is 40 kHz and bursting time \(t_b=3\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm s\). Find a and film thickness h.
C.1. Closed-bottle pressure

A bottle holds total CO2 amount nT=0.2 mol, liquid volume VL=750 mL and gas headspace VG=25 mL containing only CO2. Find equilibrium pressure at 6 and 20 degrees Celsius.
C.2. Expansion temperature and fog
For all subsequent parts use Pi=4.69 bar at 6 degrees Celsius and 7.45 bar at 20 degrees Celsius. The gas expands reversibly and adiabatically to P0. Calculate the final temperatures without phase change. Solid CO2 saturation follows \(\log_{10}(P_{sat}^{CO_2}/P_0)=6.81-1300/(T-3.49)\). Identify grey-white water fog or blue CO2-crystal fog for each initial temperature, assuming the two stated fog mechanisms are exclusive.
C.3. Cork maximum height
At 6 degrees Celsius use Pi=4.69 bar. A cork has mass 10 g, diameter d=1.8 cm, and initially inserted length l0=2.5 cm. Friction is alpha times its contact area. Initially the pressure force barely exceeds friction. Find the maximum rise after exit, neglecting net gas pressure thereafter.

children.text: For one liquid-gas interface the Laplace pressure jump is \[P_b=P_0+2\sigma/a.\]
Growth requires \(c_\ell>k_H(P_0+2\sigma/a)\). Thus \[a_c=\frac{2\sigma c_0}{P_0(c_\ell-c_0)}.\] At cl=4c0, ac=2sigma/(3P0)=0.313 micrometres.

The ideal-gas moles are \(n_c=4\pi a^3P_0/(3RT_0)\). Since \(\dot n_c=4\pi a^2j\), \(\dot a=jRT_0/P_0\). Consequently \[a^2=a_0^2+2DRT_0(c_\ell-c_0)t/P_0\] in model 1, and \[a=a_0+KRT_0(c_\ell-c_0)t/P_0\] in model 2. The measured radius grows linearly at about \(q_a=0.24\,\mathrm{mm/s}\), selecting model 2. For cl=4c0, \(K=q_a/(3k_HRT_0)\simeq1.0\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m/s}\). The source marking range omits its power-of-ten factor in one line.

Buoyancy is \(4\pi a^3\rho_\ell g_0/3\), downward weight is \(4\pi a^3\rho_g g_0/3\), and viscous drag is downward. Since gas density is small, \[v\simeq2\rho_\ell g_0a^2/(9\eta).\] Neighbour spacing divided by \(1/f_b\) estimates speed at a measured radius. Representative graph measurements a about 0.20 mm and v about 4.5 cm/s give \(\eta\sim2\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{Pa\,s}\). Pair the measured radius and spacing consistently.

Use \(dz/da=v/q_a=2\rho_\ell g_0a^2/(9\eta q_a)\). Integrating gives \[H_\ell=2\rho_\ell g_0(a_H^3-a_0^3)/(27\eta q_a).\] Neglecting a0, \(a_H=[27\eta q_aH_\ell/(2\rho_\ell g_0)]^{1/3}\simeq0.40\,\mathrm{mm}\) for viscosity 0.002 Pa s.

The bubble gas-volume outflow is \((4\pi/3)a_H^3N_bf_b\). Using A.5 this is \(18\pi\eta q_aH_\ell N_bf_b/(\rho_\ell g_0)\). Convert volume to moles by P0/(RT0) and use \(q_a=KRT_0(c_\ell-c_0)/P_0\): \[\frac{dc_\ell}{dt}=-\frac{18\pi N_bf_b\eta KH_\ell}{\rho_\ell g_0V_\ell}(c_\ell-c_0),\quad\tau=\frac{\rho_\ell g_0V_\ell}{18\pi N_bf_b\eta KH_\ell}.\] It is the excess concentration above c0 that decays exponentially.
An area increase dA removes surface energy \(2\sigma dA\). Half, \(\sigma dA\), becomes kinetic energy \(\rho_\ell h\,dA\,v_f^2/2\). Thus \[v_f=\sqrt{2\sigma/(\rho_\ell h)}.\]
Adiabatic pressure is \(P=P_0[V_0/(V_0+Sz)]^\gamma\simeq P_0(1-\gamma Sz/V_0)\). Thus \(m_p\ddot z=-\gamma P_0S^2z/V_0\), giving \[f_0=\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{\gamma P_0S^2}{m_pV_0}}.\]

Substitute \(S=\pi r_c^2\) into B.2 and eliminate rc. This gives \[a=\frac{3\sqrt3\gamma P_0}{64\pi\rho_gf_{max}^2}\sqrt{\frac{\rho_\ell g_0}{\sigma}}\simeq0.53\,\mathrm{mm}.\] Then rc is about 0.15 mm and \(v_f=r_c/t_b\simeq5\,\mathrm{m/s}\). Finally \(h=2\sigma/(\rho_\ell v_f^2)\simeq3.7\,\mu\mathrm m\).

Conservation with Henry law gives \(n_T=k_HP_iV_L+P_iV_G/(RT_0)\), hence \[P_i=\frac{n_T}{k_HV_L+V_G/(RT_0)}.\] The pressures are about 4.81 bar at 6 C and 7.76 bar at 20 C. These are distinct from the pressures explicitly supplied for the following questions.

Adiabatic expansion gives \(T_f=T_0(P_0/P_i)^{(\gamma-1)/\gamma}\). This gives approximately 195 K from 6 C, and 184 K from 20 C. The CO2 sublimation temperature at one bar from the supplied law is approximately 194.4 K. Thus the 6 C case stays just above sublimation and produces the stated grey-white water fog. The 20 C case crosses below sublimation and produces blue CO2-crystal fog. In the multiple-choice wording, statements 1 and 4 are true. Once crystallization occurs, latent heat modifies the no-transition temperature estimate.

Initial balance gives \(\alpha\simeq(P_i-P_0)d/(4\ell_0)\). During extraction at height z, friction is \(\alpha\pi d(\ell_0-z)\), with work \(W_f=-(P_i-P_0)\pi d^2\ell_0/8\). Put \(\Delta V=\pi d^2\ell_0/4\). Adiabatic gas work is \[W_g=\frac{P_iV_G}{\gamma-1}\left[1-\left(\frac{V_G}{V_G+\Delta V}\right)^{\gamma-1}\right].\] Atmospheric work is \(-P_0\Delta V\). The exit kinetic energy is approximately \(W_g+W_f-P_0\Delta V\), about 0.76 J, ignoring small gravitational work during extraction as in the source. Free-flight rise is this divided by mg0, approximately 7.7 m. Including the cork weight in initial friction balance and extraction changes the result slightly, rather than changing the dominant gas-energy calculation.
